Burning cost of an excess of loss layer

Source: R/reinsurance_pricing.R
burning_cost.Rd

Experience rating of a layer of limit excess of deductible: the past large losses are brought to the money of the rating year, put through the layer as if it had been in force, developed to ultimate and divided by the premium of their year, brought to the rating year's rates.

Usage

burning_cost(
  losses,
  premium,
  deductible,
  limit,
  aggregate_deductible = 0,
  aggregate_limit = Inf,
  inflation = 0,
  rating_year = NULL,
  development = 1,
  premium_index = 1,
  threshold = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  weights = c("premium", "equal"),
  rating_premium = NULL
)

Arguments

losses

A data frame of the large losses with the columns year and amount (in the money of their year); other columns, such as a claim number, are kept.

premium

The subject premium of each year: a data frame with the columns year and premium, or numbers named by year. Its years are those of the experience; a year without losses has none in the layer.

deductible, limit

The layer, limit (or Inf) excess of deductible, for each loss.

aggregate_deductible, aggregate_limit

The annual aggregate deductible and limit of the layer's losses; the aggregate limit is often the limit times one plus the number of reinstatements.

inflation

An annual rate (0.05 for 5%) or index values named by year, including the rating year.

rating_year

The year being priced; by default the year after the last.

development

One factor for all years, one per year, or factors named by year, applied to each year's layer losses. Defaults to 1.

premium_index

The factor that brings each year's premium to the rating year's rates and exposure, as development. Defaults to 1.

threshold

The reporting threshold of the losses, used for the warning; NULL (the default) for none.

exclude

Years left out of the burning cost (they are still shown).

weights

"premium" (the default) for the total layer losses over the total on-level premium, or "equal" for the mean of the years' burning costs.

rating_premium

The subject premium of the rating year; the expected layer loss is the burning cost times it. NULL (the default) gives no expected loss.

Value

An object of class netsimr_burning_cost, a list with by_year (each year's number of losses and of losses in the layer, its indexed losses, layer losses, development, developed and aggregate layer losses, premium, premium index, on-level premium, burning cost and whether it is included, and, with rating_premium, the layer losses at the rating year's premium), losses (each loss indexed and in the layer), rate (the burning cost), expected_loss, rating_year, rating_premium, n_layer_losses (in the years included) and the layer.

Details

Each loss is indexed to the rating year with inflation, and its part in the layer, \(\min(\max(x - d, 0), l)\), taken. Each year's layer losses are multiplied by its development factor (for the late reported claims and the development of the known ones, e.g. from chain_ladder), and then the aggregate deductible and limit apply. The burning cost of a year is its layer losses over its subject premium times its premium_index (the on-level premium). The burning cost of the layer is the total over the total, weighting years by premium, or the mean of the years' rates.

Losses are usually given above a reporting threshold. A loss just below the threshold, indexed, reaches the layer when the indexed threshold exceeds the deductible; a warning names the years where it does.

See also

pareto_rating, property_exposure_rating and technical_premium.

Other reinsurance pricing functions: credibility_weight(), mbbefd_curve(), pareto_rating(), property_exposure_rating(), technical_premium()

Examples

bc <- burning_cost(xl_large_losses, xl_premium[, c("year", "premium")],
                   deductible = 1e6, limit = 4e6, inflation = 0.04,
                   development = setNames(xl_premium$development, xl_premium$year),
                   premium_index = setNames(xl_premium$rate_index, xl_premium$year),
                   threshold = 5e5, rating_premium = 60e6)
bc
#> Burning cost of 4,000,000 xs 1,000,000 for 2025
#>   Years:              10 (2015 to 2024)
#>   Losses in the layer: 25 
#>   Burning cost:       4.972% of subject premium (premium weighted)
#>   Expected layer loss: 2,983,162 
bc$by_year[, c("year", "layer_losses", "onlevel_premium", "burning_cost")]
